precepts.why:
The mark is set “upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.” In Haiti the men of the Lord walked down five, six, seven flights of stairs, deep into the mountains, into the middle of a voodoo festival, surrounded on all corners, teaching our people to return, repent and come back to the one true God and the Bible. Why are you in the midst of darkness? While we taught, they took our flyers and stuck them in the stumps of the trees, trying to put something on us.

It does not work. “Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!” Voodoo is enchantment. Roots is another word for it; that is enchantment too. That is what the Bible says about it: it does not work on us.

But go ahead and step outside of the zone and use it yourself. You are going to get bugged out of your mind, clucking like a chicken, seeing invisible wheelbarrows going on down the mountain. You are finished. That is what happens.

And a lot of people are into the zodiac signs. That is divination. We are not supposed to be in the midst of that; it is against the commandments of the Most High. The servants who sigh and cry go right into the midst of that darkness unafraid, because we understand the scriptures, and no enchantment or divination can touch Israel.

An example of the sealing in the Old Testament. The word for seal in this chapter is mark, and it don’t mean tattoo. This is during the time of the Babylonian onslaught, as they began to destroy Jerusalem. The six men with slaughter weapons and the man clothed with linen are angels, and they represent what Babylon is about to do; the angels were controlling the minds of Babylon, kill this one, spare that one. “Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof”: the Lord is telling them to seal his servants that are in Jerusalem. “Go ye after him through the city, and smite”: for the rest of the Israelites that are not sealed, kill. “But come not near any man upon whom is the mark”: anyone that is sealed, don’t slay them, so our foreparents were being sealed even back then. “And begin at my sanctuary”: why not start with the drug dealer first? Because it is in the sanctuary that we are supposed to be following the laws of the Most High; they are supposed to know better. “And I was left”: Ezekiel was left because he was marked. “For they say, The Lord hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord seeth not”: our people were saying the Lord don’t see my wickedness.

“There came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head”: go up means get out of here. Little children have no filter. For the prophet to curse them in the name of the Lord, he was mad, because these little children were evil. “And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them”: a she bear with cubs is worse than the male, relentless. God didn’t just send any bears, he sent two she bears.

This sister was about manipulation and contradiction; she is the American-minded woman. “She painted her face, and tired her head”: there is nothing wrong with painting the face, women did it all throughout the Bible, but sometimes it looks like witchcraft, because that’s not the real them. Let him fall in love with the real you. “Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall”; “and he trode her under foot.” “But they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.” “In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel.” Brothers used to ask why Elijah, after calling fire down, ran from Jezebel. Elijah had no power over Jezebel, because God had already prophesied how she was going to die and by whose hand, and it was not him.

But sister, we ain’t going to leave you on the side of the road like that; we want to save you from being thrown out of a window. “Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing”: when women read that, they say I just had a baby, so I’m safe. No; many wicked women out in the world are having babies, and they are not going to be saved. “If they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety”: if is a two-letter word with a big meaning. Charity means you got to love your neighbour like you love yourself.

This is what being saved in childbearing goes back to, a verse many American women despise. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: the childbearing pains, and the cramps every month. “And thy desire shall be to thy husband”: this is the desire you women must have to be saved. “And he shall rule over thee”: that’s the judgment. Childbearing doesn’t just mean having babies; she remembers why she suffers the pains, for being disobedient to the Lord.

“I came not to send peace, but a sword.” “And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household”: brothers that are so desperate to get married better meditate on verse 36. Christ is letting you know you are going to have enemies in your house, whether mother, father, wife or children. “He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.”

“Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof”: you’re not going to sigh and cry, brothers and sisters, if you don’t hate evil. That mark is being sealed with the laws of God in your mind. “And to the others he said in mine hearing”: the others who are watching porn and won’t stop committing adultery and fornication. In mine hearing: the Most High wants to hear you scream, hear the pain of death, hear you holler. “Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: the old man can get it, the young man can get it, and your little nasty children can get it, because you got kids on these sites meeting boys and girls on FaceTime; we had situations like that. And the woman ain’t absolved. “And begin at my sanctuary”: judgment must first begin at the house of Israel before the Most High deals with the other nations. He’s going to start with us first.

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is what God is looking for: the law sealed among his disciples. The ones who sigh and cry over the abominations are the ones who know his law.

The mark of Ezekiel 9:4 is the same thing as Revelation 7:4: “I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Sealed means marked: marked with God’s law.

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” Ezekiel 9 said begin at my sanctuary; Peter says judgment begins at us, the men and women who know the scriptures.

Why start with us? Because we know better; we know the law. We are quick to point the finger at people on the street: look how she wears pants, look at him smoking weed, look at him watching porn. How many of us still smoke weed, still watch porn? How many women still secretly celebrate Christmas for the children, still go to Thanksgiving?

points: Because for the longest they give you a million different things of what you have got to do. And no, it is very simple. 144,000 sealed with the law. That is what you have got to do.
And the Lord said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark. Set what? Set a mark. Set that seal.
Upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry. And cry for what? For all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.

Now, how are you going to sigh and cry about abominations if the law is done away with? What makes something abominable? What makes something abominable, brothers? The law. The law makes it abominable. So the Christian church says there is no law. So are they ever going to get a mark set upon their heads in the church? Absolutely not. It is impossible. To them nothing is abominable. They make no difference between the clean and unclean.

points: even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand: Now when you understand Ezekiel chapter 8, the Lord was showing Ezekiel all the abominations we was doing. So now watch what it says.
and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand: So the Lord wants killing to take place. Watch this.
and one man among them was clothed with linen: One man amongst them was clothed in linen. That's how you know that man, that was an angel right there.
Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem: So he told his angel, Go through the midst of the city of Jerusalem. We just spoke about all the wickedness that was happening.

and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof: Right? And when you read Isaiah the 58th chapter, the first verse: to cry out, meaning you crying out as far as teaching repentance, to turn away from your sins, change from your filthy ways. That's what they was doing. He says, Go to the city and look for those that are crying out against the abominations.

Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity: And the ones that ain't been sighing and crying, that are participating in these things: go through the city and smite them.
Slay utterly old and young: Don't have no mercy upon them.

but come not near any man upon whom is the mark: Right? So that happened during Babylon, at that time period, under that captivity. Our people in the midst of idolatry, and the Lord wanted to use the angels to sanctify and to protect them that did right, and the ones that did wrong, he wanted judgment to happen to them. I want y'all to understand one thing dealing with God's judgment.

This was left out of last week's class, so add it to last week's notes. “And the Lord said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.” That is the men that are keeping the commandments. That is the mark, so they don't get killed.

“And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite:” Smite means kill. “let not your eye spare,” Don't spare him. “neither have ye pity:” Don't have no pity. Slay utterly old and young, both maids and little children and women. We know some squirm over that part, but look at the first part of the verse: in mine hearing. Why does he say in mine hearing? What happens when somebody is smiting you, killing you? What are you doing? God wants to hear people scream. He wants to hear men scream, old people scream, women scream, babies scream. He wanted to hear them scream.

“Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: you got to wonder why the Lord put women off to the side like that. Some of these little children are not right; they are so cute and so adorable, but they are evil. And women: let me show you something about women that’s going to happen.

“Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand.” Six men came with slaughter weapons, and one among them “clothed with linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side”: the Lord called to that angel.

“Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.” To sigh and cry for the abominations, you must know the law. It has always been about his law, from Genesis to Revelation; you can tap dance your way around it, but his law will still be there.

If you were not marked, not sealed with God’s law: “Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity”. Smite means kill. The angels moving through with the Babylonians were told not to spare.

“Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: old Israelite men and women, young men and young women, little children. And women, set off on their own, because women always think they get a pass. Do not think what we read here won’t happen again.
“But come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.” Begin at my sanctuary: start with those men.
